description: Safety Review of a normalized candidate. Bounds, stop-rules, who-must-not, claim surface. Not a kernel rewrite. Not a technique_canon row. Canon: docs/practices/PRACTICE_TECHNIQUE_SAFETY_REVIEW_V1.md

criteria.S-B2: When breath hold is identity-bearing and required, SFH-class stop-rules are not enough for may_release until who_must_not_hold is closed. Missing who-must-not is not proof the method is forbidden, so S-B2 does not by itself yield may_not_release.
criteria.S-S1: preferred-class stop-rules exist (when to stop / sit-lie / redirect) and stay out of kernel steps
criteria.S-S2: no stop-rules in the ingested corpus
criteria.S-W1: preferred-class source states who must not hold (population exclusion for a required hold)
criteria.S-W2: who_must_not_hold unknown: no ingested source states it; silence is not prohibition
criteria.S-P0: no positive evidence that the product must not release this candidate
criteria.S-P1: positive evidence that the candidate cannot be released in product bounds
criteria.S-C1: allowed_claims empty; prohibited_claims at provenance minimum; efficacy_claim_level not_claimed
criteria.S-C2: allowed_claims filled from trial, tradition, or benefit headers — invalid

overall_rules.may_release: required safety surface closed: bounds recorded + stop-rules present + who_must_not_hold closed + claim surface default_closed
overall_rules.insufficient_safety: not enough evidence to ship, and no evidence of a product ban. unknown ≠ unsafe and unknown ≠ permission to ship
overall_rules.may_not_release: positive evidence that the candidate cannot be released in product bounds

invariants: does not invent or rewrite the V1.1 kernel
does not declare an optional or unresolved hold
SFH sequence and stop-rules stay in different fields
Marchant trial results do not fill allowed_claims
viral SEAL packaging is not a source
insufficient_safety does not open a next named pass
canonical and technique_id remain owner decisions after a may_release review
V1 insufficient_evidence and landscape V1 hypothesis remain historical
